# openrouter_guardrail_policy_member_assignment (Resource)

Assigns one typed guardrail policy to one organization member, and removes the assignment when the resource is destroyed.

A policy that is not the workspace default does nothing until it is assigned. `openrouter_guardrail_policy_budget`, `openrouter_guardrail_policy_moderation` and `openrouter_guardrail_policy_model_availability` create the policies; this resource attaches one of them to a member. A member holds at most one policy of each type: the route sets the assignment for a policy type rather than adding to it, so assigning a second policy of the same type to the same member displaces the first. Different types are independent, so a member can hold one of each and that is one resource each; two resources of one type on one member would displace each other on every apply. A policy's own member_ids and api_key_hashes attributes name the same membership from the policy side, so declare one side or the other for a given subject and policy: competing declarations of one membership overwrite each other on alternate applies.

A policy a member inherits from the workspace default is not an assignment and is not managed here. The read returns the directly assigned policies and the inherited ones separately, and only the directly assigned list is compared, so a member that inherits a policy without holding it does not read as drift.

The API changes assignments one policy at a time and requires the state the caller last read, answering 409 once that state has moved. The provider reads before every write and reads again after the first conflict, so an assignment attached or removed elsewhere between two applies is reconciled rather than fought over, and a second conflict in a row is reported with the API's own message instead of retried indefinitely. A destroy of an assignment that is already gone is a no-op rather than a failure. Creating a resource for an assignment that is already in place adopts it without writing, and destroying it removes the assignment whoever put it there, so an assignment is not owned by the configuration that declares it.

Changing `member_id`, `policy_id` or `policy_type` replaces the resource: the destroy removes the old assignment and the create makes the new one. A policy cannot be moved between workspaces; where state records a workspace_id, changing it plans a replacement instead, and removing `workspace_id` from configuration is refused at plan time because the read that follows needs that scope. `workspace_id` is required for an organization management key and may be omitted for a workspace-scoped key, which defaults to its own workspace. It is a UUID in every case: the routes that take a scope validate the field as one, so a workspace slug is refused with 400 `Invalid guardrail policy request`, the same answer an omitted scope gets, rather than being looked up. This resource's own update path never reaches the API, because a change to the scope plans a replacement.

Import takes `<member_id>/<policy_type>/<policy_id>`, or `<workspace_id>/<member_id>/<policy_type>/<policy_id>` for an organization management key. The stored `id` is the bare form, so importing it under an organization management key means adding the workspace prefix; the API never returns the workspace, and a read that reaches the route without one is refused rather than scoped to a default.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "openrouter_guardrail_policy_budget" "engineering" {
  name         = "Engineering monthly budget"
  policy_type  = "budget"
  workspace_id = "3f7c2a4e-9b1d-4c6e-8a2f-5d0e1b7c9a31"

  config = {
    include_byok_in_budgets = false
    limit_usd               = 100
    reset_interval          = "monthly"
  }
}

data "openrouter_organization_members" "all" {}

locals {
  # Name the member the assignment is for. The member list is not ordered, so an
  # index would attach the policy to whoever happens to come first; matching the
  # address and taking one result fails when the member is absent or the address
  # matches more than one, rather than assigning the policy to the wrong person.
  engineering_lead = one([
    for member in data.openrouter_organization_members.all.data :
    member.id if member.email == "lead@example.com"
  ])
}

# The assignment is what makes the policy apply to the member: a policy on its
# own constrains nothing.
resource "openrouter_guardrail_policy_member_assignment" "example" {
  member_id    = local.engineering_lead
  policy_id    = openrouter_guardrail_policy_budget.engineering.id
  policy_type  = openrouter_guardrail_policy_budget.engineering.policy_type
  workspace_id = openrouter_guardrail_policy_budget.engineering.workspace_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `member_id` (String) Organization member user ID to assign the policy to. Requires replacement if changed.
- `policy_id` (String) ID of the policy to assign, for example `openrouter_guardrail_policy_moderation.example.id`. Requires replacement if changed.
- `policy_type` (String) Type of the policy being assigned: `budget`, `model_availability`, `moderation` or `rate_limit`. Must match the policy's own type. Requires replacement if changed.

### Optional

- `workspace_id` (String) Workspace the policy belongs to. Required for an organization management key; a workspace-scoped key defaults to its own workspace and gets 403 for any other.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Import identifier of the assignment, `<member_id>/<policy_type>/<policy_id>`. Importing under an organization management key needs the workspace prefix, which this stored identifier does not include.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = openrouter_guardrail_policy_member_assignment.example
  id = "3f7c2a4e-9b1d-4c6e-8a2f-5d0e1b7c9a31/user_2abcDEFghiJKLmnoPQRstu/budget/8b2e6f1a-4c3d-4e5f-9a7b-1c2d3e4f5a6b"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is <member_id>/<policy_type>/<policy_id>, or
# <workspace_id>/<member_id>/<policy_type>/<policy_id> for an organization
# management key, which has no workspace of its own to fall back to.
terraform import openrouter_guardrail_policy_member_assignment.example "user_2abcDEFghiJKLmnoPQRstu/budget/8b2e6f1a-4c3d-4e5f-9a7b-1c2d3e4f5a6b"
```
